message.reasoning:
The user says: "start Docker on window using docker start." They want to start Docker on Windows using docker start. They likely want to run a command to start Docker service. But "docker start" is used to start containers, not the Docker daemon. To start Docker Desktop, you might need to start the Docker Desktop application or the Docker service. On Windows, you can use "net start com.docker.service" or "Start-Service Docker". Or if using Docker Desktop, you can run "docker-machine start default" if using Docker Machine. But the user says "start Docker on window using docker start." That seems ambiguous. They might want to start Docker Desktop via command line. There's no direct "docker start" to start the Docker engine. But you can start the Docker service via PowerShell: Start-Service Docker. Or via CMD: net start com.docker.service. Or if using Docker Desktop, you can run "docker-machine start default" if using Docker Machine.

We have a tool to execute commands on Windows. We can call the function to run a command. But we need to decide what command to run. The user wants to start Docker on Windows. So we can run "net start com.docker.service" or "Start-Service Docker". Let's choose "net start com.docker.service" because it's simpler. Or we can use "Start-Service Docker" in PowerShell. But the tool expects a Windows command line instruction. It can accept multiple commands separated by &&. So we can do "net start com.docker.service". That will start the Docker service. If Docker Desktop is installed, it may start automatically. But we can try.

Thus we will call the function with command "net start com.docker.service".
